subject: Strategic capacity allocation & price-protection request
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.r@acmehealth.com>

Cc: cloudscale-sales@cloudscale.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal + price protection ask

Mina / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme is moving toward a production rollout for our patient-facing summarization use case and we are ready to discuss a reserved capacity commitment. High-level ask below:

- Target: 80 x A100-equivalent GPU reserved for 12 months (steady-state), with a 3-month ramp window.
- Preferred commercial: fixed monthly fee for reserved capacity + overage per token.
- Risk ask: because we are a regulated customer with predictable budget windows, procurement needs a price-protection clause that limits upward movement tied to the GPU spot/index. We can accept an indexation mechanism, but need a floor and cap to avoid surprise increases.

Attached: Acme_Commit_Term_Sheet.pdf and GPU-price-index-model.xlsx (simple sensitivity model we ran).

Specific request: Can Redwood provide a conditional discount / price cushion if market GPU costs increase >15% vs current pricing, and a floor protection so our effective unit cost won't rise more than 12% in the first 9 months? Procurement needs to know what approvals you would require for any exceptional concessions.

Please let me know your standard approach and ideally a sample clause we can share with our legal/purchasing. We are aiming to sign a term sheet by end of month.

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_Commit_Term_Sheet.pdf (application/pdf, 112KB); GPU-price-index-model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

Thanks Mina — reviewed Acme's model and ran quick scenarios. High-level thoughts:

- For a 12-month commit at ~80 GPUs the economics thin if we absorb more than a ~10-12% increase in underlying GPU cost.
- Proposed commercial fallback we can offer without exec escalation: a conditional protection that limits customer OPEX increase to 10% (floor protection) for the first 6 months and includes an automatic reprice review for months 7-12 if the index changes >12%.
- For anything beyond a 12% customer protection request (e.g., their requested 12% floor + further concessions), we need Finance sign-off and a limited executive credit reserve.
- Suggest we couple the protection with a 10% flex-bucket (unreserved burst capacity billed at a higher overage rate) so Redwood can auto-scale without permanent capacity commitments. This reduces downside.

Action items:
- Karthik: can you propose draft language for the index clause? Keep it simple: reference a published GPU index + quarterly reconciliation and a cap-trigger step-up to negotiations.
- Grace: can you run the +20% GPU cost P&L in the attached model and mark the tolerance for a 12-month term?

If we can do the limited protection + flex bucket, we should be able to present a single-sheet commercial counter to Acme and avoid long procurement back-and-forth.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-exec-note.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity proposal + price protection ask

Draft clause (for internal review):

"Price Indexation and Protection: Customer rates for reserved capacity will be set based on Redwood's published list price at execution. Quarterly, Redwood will reconcile changes to a mutually-agreed GPU cost index (published by CloudScale Intelligence). If the index increases by more than 10% quarter-over-quarter, Redwood will initiate a reconciliation that may include an adjustment to overage rates or reserved fees, subject to a cap of a 12% effective customer-rate increase over any rolling 9-month period. Any adjustment beyond the 12% cap will require written approval from Redwood Finance and Sales Leadership. For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood may offer a one-time credit or transitional discount that is at Redwood's discretion and requires executive sign-off."

Operational notes:
- Recommend we include a 10% flex bucket for burst (no reservation) at +35% overage rate.
- Also include a termination-for-convenience breakpoint after month 6 with 60 days' notice and a predefined unwind fee to mitigate stranded-cost risk.

This language keeps us protected and gives Acme the predictability they want without open-ended exposure. If Finance is comfortable with the 12% cap we can send a counter.

Karthik Iyer
Contracts & Pricing | Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the model. We've discussed internally and can put the following counter on paper for your procurement/legal review: 

Counter (high level):
- Commitment: 70 reserved GPUs for 12 months (3-month ramp).
- Commercial: fixed monthly reserved fee + standard overage. We will provide a 10% upfront commitment discount in exchange for the 12-month term.
- Price protection: Redwood will reference the CloudScale GPU Index quarterly. If the index increases >10% in any quarter, Redwood will initiate a reconciliation. Customer effective rate increases will be capped at 12% over any rolling 9-month window. Any adjustment beyond that cap requires Redwood Finance + Sales Leadership approval (we will provide written notice and a reconciliation schedule).
- Flex: 10% burst capacity available at higher overage rates to cover spikes without increasing reserved footprint.
- Breakpoint: mutual review at month 6; early unwind option with defined unwind fee to protect Redwood from stranded capacity cost.

Next steps: I can send a one-page commercial term sheet and a DocuSign for the Acme PO if this framework is acceptable. If you accept the 70-GPU baseline versus your original 80, we can preserve more of our cost buffer while meeting Acme's predictability needs.

Attached: redwood-pricing-exec-note.docx (internal briefing) — I will share a cleaned counterparty-term sheet for legal review if you confirm the approach.

Would love a quick call today or tomorrow to align before we formalize.

Best,
